newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: NEDLLOYD, P&O in container merger.
newsitem.headline: NEDLLOYD, P&O in container merger.

text.p: Nedlloyd NV and Britain's Penninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Company Plc said on Monday they planned a complete merger of their container shipping businesses.

The two companies said they would each take a 50 percent stake in the merged company, to be called P&O Nedlloyd Container Line, with Nedlloyd making a payment of $175 million to P&O to equalise the shareholdings.
"With a combined turnover of nearly $4.0 billion and a net asset value of some $1.5 billion, the new company will be one of the largest in world container shipping," a joint statement said.
P&O Nedlloyd will have an eight strong board, jointly chaired by Lord Sterling of P&O and Leo Berndsen of Nedlloyd.
It will begin operations no later than December 31, 1996, following due diligence and regulatory procedures.

P&O Nedlloyd will have the world's biggest container ship fleet in terms of standing slots and an annual throughput of close to 2.5 million twenty foot equivalent units (TEU). The TEU is the standard measure of volume in container shipping.
The new firm will operate 112 owned and chartered container ships and 540,000 TEU owned and leased container boxes.

The companies said savings of over $200 million a year have already been identified from a total $3.9 billion cost base. The savings will be achieved by reducing the combined workforce of around 9,400 to approximately 8,000, greater network efficiency and reduced inland and terminal costs.
Berndsen, chairman of Koninklijke Nedlloyd Groep NV, said in a statement: "This new company will have the required scale to compete successfully throughout the world."

Sterling, executive chairman of P&O said: "The new company will have an excellent management team and a strong balance sheet. P&O Nedlloyd will be a world force in container shipping." -- Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
